jobs.title: Corporate FP&A Manager
jobs.description:
About Snorkel

Snorkel AI is the frontier AI data lab, helping teams build the data and environments behind high-performing frontier and agentic AI. We combine technology with research-driven AI data development to create datasets, benchmarks, evals, and custom solutions for real-world AI systems. Founded out of the Stanford AI Lab in 2019, Snorkel works with leading AI labs and enterprises to move from better data to better outcomes.

Excited to help us redefine how AI is built? Apply to be the newest Snorkeler!

The Role

The Corporate FP&A Manager will own headcount and operating expense planning across Snorkel and serve as the finance partner to department leaders. You will turn hiring and spending plans into reliable forecasts, help teams make investment decisions and build better cost visibility. You will also manage Ramp and procurement workflows and implement planning tools as the business grows.

Key Responsibilities

- Lead annual department budgets and rolling forecasts for headcount and non-headcount expenses, aligning spending with company growth and profitability targets.

- Own the headcount and personnel cost model with People and Recruiting, reflecting hiring plans, attrition, compensation and benefits.

- Partner with department leaders on hiring and investment decisions, identifying cost savings and evaluating tradeoffs in growth, capacity and profitability.

- Partner with Accounting on month-end close, including expense accruals, and lead headcount and OpEx variance analysis against budget and forecast.

- Own SaaS and vendor spend tracking, the purchase order system and procurement approvals, working with Legal, IT and Accounting on purchases and renewals.

- Own and manage Ramp, including spend programs, company cards, approval workflows and expense policies, in partnership with Accounting.

- Implement and administer planning tools such as Pigment or Anaplan and improve data integrations, reporting and planning processes.

- Partner with the Senior FP&A Manager to prepare consolidated financial reporting, with clear commentary on spending trends and outlook for executive reviews and board materials.

About You

- 5+ years of FP&A or business finance experience, including direct ownership of headcount and operating expense planning in a growing technology company.

- Advanced Excel and Google Sheets skills and experience building models that connect hiring, vendor commitments and operating drivers to financial forecasts.

- Hands-on experience managing Ramp, including spend approvals, expense controls and reporting.

- Experience implementing and administering planning systems such as Pigment, Anaplan or similar platforms, including financial model design and data integrations.

- Strong understanding of expense accruals, cost allocation and financial statements, with a record of partnering effectively with Accounting.

- Ability to build relationships with department leaders, explain financial tradeoffs clearly and turn analysis into recommendations.

- Strong attention to detail and the ability to establish practical processes, improve data quality and follow through across multiple workstreams.

Experience with SaaS or AI businesses, IT, cloud or inference costs, and contractor or services delivery economics is a plus.

Why This Role

This role is an opportunity to build the cost planning and spend management foundation of a growing AI company. You will help leaders make better hiring and investment decisions and translate operational improvements into stronger financial performance.
Actual compensation will be determined based on factors including skills, qualifications, experience, and geographic location.

Salary range(s) for this role
$125,000 — $180,000 USD

Be Your Best at Snorkel

Joining Snorkel AI means becoming part of a company that has market proven solutions, robust funding, and is scaling rapidly—offering a unique combination of stability and the excitement of high growth. As a member of our team, you’ll have meaningful opportunities to shape priorities and initiatives, influence key strategic decisions, and directly impact our ongoing success. Whether you’re looking to deepen your technical expertise, explore leadership opportunities, or learn new skills across multiple functions, you’re fully supported in building your career in an environment designed for growth, learning, and shared success.

Snorkel AI is proud to be an Equal Employment Opportunity employer and is committed to building a team that represents a variety of backgrounds, perspectives, and skills. Snorkel AI embraces diversity and provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment. Snorkel AI prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type on the basis of race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local law. All employment is decided on the basis of qualifications, performance, merit, and business need.

About the Role

We are hiring a Senior Strategy & Operations Manager to help run Snorkel's rapidly scaling Data-as-a-Service (DaaS) business. DaaS Operations is the centralized Strategy & Operations team reporting into the Head of Strategy and Operations, partnering across Supply, Delivery, GTM, Innovation, Finance, and Engineering to keep the business running with rigor and scaling efficiently as complexity grows.

In this role, you will move fluidly across the most important problems in the business — operating cadences and planning cycles, capacity and supply planning, project execution and quality, customer outcomes, and the new operating functions we are standing up as DaaS scales. You will own end-to-end workstreams that don't have a clear home, build the operating systems behind them, and partner closely with the leaders of each function to turn strategy into measurable execution.

This is a high-impact role suited for a strong operator who thrives in ambiguity, brings structure to fast-moving environments, and can balance strategic thinking with hands-on execution.

What You'll Do

- Partner with leaders across DaaS — Supply, Delivery, GTM, Innovation, Finance, and Engineering — to bring operational clarity, execution rigor, and alignment to their highest-priority initiatives

- Own the operating cadence of the business — weekly, monthly, and quarterly reviews — and ensure goals, metrics, and reporting tell a clear story to leadership

- Drive cross-functional initiatives end-to-end, especially the ones that span multiple teams or sit in the gaps between them

- Lead annual planning and quarterly business review inputs across DaaS, translating strategic priorities into structured operating plans and measurable milestones

- Diagnose performance issues across the business — capacity, quality, throughput, customer outcomes, cost — and partner with the right function to fix them

- Step in to own ambiguous workstreams or new problem areas as they emerge, and drive them to outcomes

- Improve operational processes and build durable systems that reduce friction and increase throughput as the business scales

- Identify execution risks early and proactively surface trade-offs to leadership

- Serve as a thought partner and executor to DaaS leadership and adjacent teams

Qualifications

- 7+ years of experience in strategy, operations, consulting, or similar roles

- Experience partnering closely with operational leaders in high-growth or complex environments

- Demonstrated ability to drive cross-functional initiatives and deliver outcomes end-to-end

- Strong analytical skills with comfort using data to inform decisions and track performance

- Ability to bring structure and clarity to ambiguous problem spaces

- Proven track record of influencing without authority

- Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with experience presenting to senior stakeholders

- Strong prioritization skills and bias toward action

- Comfortable operating in imperfect systems while building scalable processes

- Entrepreneurial mindset with high ownership and accountability

Bonus Points

- Experience in services, marketplace, or data-driven businesses

- Exposure to delivery, operations, or workforce-based execution models

- Experience supporting planning cycles and executive reporting

jobs.description:

Excited to help us redefine how AI is built? Apply to be the newest Snorkeler!

About This Role

The Fellow Program is a critical new initiative at Snorkel AI, designed to build and scale the expert workforce powering our ability to deliver exceptional outcomes for customers. We are building the people foundation for a program that will grow through rolling cohorts, new geographies, and a potential workforce expected to scale into the thousands.

We are looking for a strategic, entrepreneurial Staff HRBP to help shape what this program becomes. This is not a traditional support role. You will own the people strategy and operating model for one of Snorkel’s most important growth initiatives, partnering directly with senior leaders to design how Fellows are hired, onboarded, developed, deployed, recognized, and supported throughout their employment lifecycle.

This is a rare 0-to-1 opportunity for a thoughtful builder who enjoys turning ambiguity into momentum. You will create the programs, practices, and manager capabilities that enable a new workforce model to scale with quality, speed, and a standout employee experience. The work you do will have a visible impact on our Fellows, our customers, and Snorkel’s ability to scale. This role is hybrid ( 3 days/week in office) in San Francisco, CA.

What You'll Do

This role reports to the Senior Director, People Programs & Partnerships, and will focus on:

- Own the people strategy and operating model for the Fellow Program, translating ambitious program goals and workforce needs into a clear, scalable people plan.

- Partner with Fellow program leadership to operationalize the strategic direction for the program’s people architecture, including performance philosophy, talent segmentation, growth pathways, manager model, bench and redeployment approach, and key lifecycle decision points.

- Partner cross-functionally to build the core people programs that make the Fellow experience exceptional, from onboarding and early-tenure support through progression, transition, and exit.

- Design a tailored performance management framework that creates clarity, accountability, and growth, including measures of performance, evaluation criteria, review cadence, feedback expectations, and manager tools.

- Create and operationalize bespoke milestone programs, including early-tenure check-ins and reviews, to assess ramp, performance, engagement, and readiness for continued placement.

- Partner with Program Leadership, Supply, and project leaders to determine how performance data, quality signals, project outcomes, and manager feedback inform talent and workforce decisions.

- Define a compelling approach to Fellow growth and mobility, including development conversations, career pathways, and identification of Fellows who may be ready for broader opportunities at Snorkel.

- Lead cross-functional decisions on workforce design, manager capacity, organizational structure, scaling approach, and global employment strategy as the program expands.

- Serve as a strategic coach to program leaders and managers, helping them navigate talent tradeoffs, performance decisions, team design, employee relations, and sensitive people matters.

- Partner closely with Recruiting, People Operations, Total Rewards, Legal, Finance, and external employment partners to deliver a cohesive, compliant, and high-quality Fellow experience.

- Build scalable processes with the right balance of rigor and speed, creating a durable foundation for the program’s long-term growth.

What We’re Looking For

- 8+ years of progressive HR Business Partner or People Partner experience, including experience leading people strategy for a complex business unit, workforce segment, or major organizational initiative.

- Deep performance management experience, including designing review processes, creating clear performance expectations, and coaching leaders through difficult performance decisions.

- Experience partnering on workforce planning, organizational design, team growth, manager effectiveness, and employee relations.

- Demonstrated ability to influence senior leaders and drive cross-functional decisions without direct authority.

- Strong judgment and comfort operating in ambiguity, with the ability to identify the right problem, develop a point of view, and move work forward.

- Experience designing workforce and talent strategies for a high-growth, operationally complex, distributed, or global employee population.

- Strong business acumen and an ability to connect people decisions to operating goals, quality outcomes, workforce capacity, and program economics.

- Excellent project management skills, with the ability to lead multiple interdependent workstreams in a fast-paced environment.

- A collaborative, low-ego approach and the ability to build trust with leaders, managers, and employees across functions.

- Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to translate complex people topics into simple, practical guidance.

Nice to Have

- Experience supporting a global, distributed, or employer-of-record workforce.

- Experience supporting an hourly, operational, services, contractor-to-employee, or other high-volume workforce model.

- Experience building talent programs for technical or AI-adjacent employee populations.

- Familiarity with using performance, quality, productivity, or project data to inform workforce and talent decisions.

jobs.title: Senior Technical Compliance Analyst
jobs.location: New York City, NY (Hybrid); San Francisco, CA (Hybrid)
jobs.description:
About Snorkel

Snorkel AI is the frontier AI data lab, helping teams build the data and environments behind high-performing frontier and agentic AI. We combine technology with research-driven AI data development to create datasets, benchmarks, evals, and custom solutions for real-world AI systems. Founded out of the Stanford AI Lab in 2019, Snorkel works with leading AI labs and enterprises to move from better data to better outcomes.

Excited to help us redefine how AI is built? Apply to be the newest Snorkeler!

Job Description

We are seeking a hands-on, builder-minded Senior Technical Compliance Analyst to serve as the operational engine behind our Trust & Security program.

You will maintain our SOC 2 Type II posture, drive our second entity from Type I to Type II, and act as the bridge between compliance requirements and engineering & delivery execution. You will also lay the technical groundwork to evolve us toward **CMMC 2.0**, ensuring we are ready for federal contracts without slowing down our product velocity.

**This is not a "compliance cop" role.** We practice **"Yes, if..."** security—you will influence architecture, automate policy enforcement, and unblock enterprise sales by ensuring the Security team has pristine, verifiable evidence at their fingertips.

What You will Do

Powering Customer Trust & Revenue Enablement

- The Engine Behind Revenue: Help drafting accurate, technically precise responses to RFPs, security questionnaires (CAIQ, SIG, custom risk assessments), and customer portals.

- Repository Stewardship: Own and continuously update the "Library of Truth"—a pristine repository of pre-vetted security evidence, technical configurations, and policy documents. By keeping this repository audit-ready, you enable the Security team to respond to enterprise prospects in hours, not days.

- Technical Depth on Demand: When a customer asks about AWS KMS encryption, logging pipelines, or IAM privilege escalation paths, you retrieve the granular evidence and draft the written narrative the Security and Legal Team needs to confidently close the deal.

Building Compliance into the DNA

- Compliance Partner: Partner with IT, Security, Product, Engineering, and Delivery early in the development lifecycle. Review new features, infrastructure changes, and vendor integrations to influence architectural decisions that bake in compliance by design—without creating friction or slowing sprints.

- Policy as Guardrails: Write, update, and operationalize security policies that accelerate delivery. Translate abstract SOC 2 and NIST controls into clear, developer-friendly tasks (e.g., IAM hardening, log retention, Zero Trust implementation).

- Compliance-as-Code: Where possible, automate policy enforcement in CI/CD pipelines so that security checks are invisible, automated, and frictionless for engineering teams.

- Enablement, Not Enforcement: Conduct lightweight compliance enablement sessions with engineering teams—showing them how to self-serve evidence collection and interpret compliance requirements—so security becomes everyone's responsibility, not just yours.

Operational GRC & Audit Excellence

- Audit Lifecycle Management: Drive and coordinate the end-to-end SOC 2 Type I and Type II audit cycles across our business entities. Manage audit schedules, coordinate with external auditors, and drive remediation of findings to keep us perpetually audit-ready.

- GRC Automation: Be the power-user of our modern GRC stack (Vanta, Drata). Automate evidence collection, continuously monitor technical controls, and eliminate manual spreadsheet tracking.

- Operational Cadences: Manage the compliance ticketing queue in Jira. Execute routine mandates including quarterly User Access Reviews (UAR), security awareness training, phishing simulations, and managing the Risk Acceptance/Exception process.

- Metrics & Reporting: Build and maintain compliance dashboards (KPIs/KRIs) for the Security Lead and executive team. Track audit readiness scores, remediation SLAs, and control health trends to provide clear visibility into our posture.

- Policy Governance: Manage the annual policy review and attestation cycle—ensuring process owners review, sign off, and update documentation on schedule, keeping our policies evergreen.

Future Federal & Supply Chain Roadmap

- Foundation for Federal Growth: Assist the Security Team in aligning current controls with federal standards—specifically NIST SP 800-53 , NIST SP 800-171 Rev 3 , FedRAMP , and CMMC 2.0 . Help draft early System Security Plans (SSPs) and Plan of Action & Milestones (POA&Ms).

- Supply Chain Risk Management (C-SCRM): Own the third-party vendor review process, assessing critical partners (Cloud, HRIS, CRM) to meet strict federal supply chain requirements and offload this operational work from the Security Lead.

- Incident Readiness: Support the Security Team during security incidents by preserving audit-relevant evidence, documenting the chronology of events, and drafting post-incident reports to satisfy regulatory and audit requirements.

Who You Are

- Experience: 7+ years of experience in technical compliance, IT audit, or GRC within a SaaS or fast-paced startup environment.

- Audit Mastery: Proven end-to-end experience supporting external SOC 2 Type I and Type II audits—with specific expertise auditing IT General Controls (ITGC) (Change Management, Logical Access, System Operations). You know how to manage auditors and translate their requests into actionable developer tasks.

- Technical Acumen: Strong understanding of modern cloud infrastructure (AWS/GCP/Azure), IAM, CI/CD pipelines, encryption standards, and vulnerability management. You can read a Terraform plan or an AWS Config rule and interpret its compliance impact.

- Tooling: Experience operating automated compliance platforms (Vanta, Drata), tracking work in Jira, and security awareness platform (KnowBe4)

- Mindset: You are a business enabler . You practice "Yes, if..." security—you negotiate secure alternatives rather than blocking releases or ignoring risks. You thrive in a partnership role, ensuring IT, Security, Engineering, and Delivery teams have everything they need to succeed.

- Communication: Exceptional written and verbal communication skills with the ability to explain technical controls to customers and business risks to engineers.

Why Join Us?

- Direct Revenue Impact: Your work directly correlates to revenue. By building the "Library of Truth," you ensure the Security team can close enterprise deals faster and more confidently.

- Be a Builder, Not a Bureaucrat: You won't just check boxes. You will build automated, scalable compliance programs that enable the business to engineer quicker and sell faster.

- Modern, Automated Tooling: Say goodbye to manual spreadsheet tracking. We leverage continuous-monitoring GRC tech so you can focus on technical risk and architecture, not admin overhead.

- Future-Proof Career Growth: Gain rare, hands-on exposure to evolving a commercial SaaS startup into a federal-ready entity (FedRAMP/CMMC), highly accelerating your market value in the GRC space.

**This role is Hybrid Only. 3 days a week in our SF or NYC office.**
Actual compensation will be determined based on factors including skills, qualifications, experience, and geographic location.

Salary range(s) for this role
$150,000 — $220,000 USD
